name: AWS Connect AI Contact Center Readiness
description: This custom lens evaluates organizational readiness for deploying AI-powered content experiences in AWS Connect Customer contact centers. It covers content strategy, knowledge base architecture, AI configuration and guardrails, content lifecycle governance, security and compliance, and operational excellence. Use this lens to identify gaps and build a roadmap for successful Connect Customer AI agents and generative AI self-service deployments.

questions.title: How do you define and manage content taxonomy and categorization standards?
questions.description: A well-defined content taxonomy ensures knowledge articles are organized consistently, enabling AI systems to locate and retrieve relevant information efficiently. Without clear categorization standards, content sprawl leads to retrieval failures and inconsistent customer experiences.

helpfulResource.displayText: Use AI agents for real-time assistance (Connect Customer admin guide)

choices.title: Established a hierarchical taxonomy aligned to customer intents and business domains

helpfulResource.displayText: Automatically categorize contacts with Connect Customer conversational analytics

improvementPlan.displayText: Define a multi-level taxonomy that maps to your top customer contact reasons. Start with intent categories (billing, technical support, account management) and subdivide into specific topics. Validate the taxonomy against real contact data from Connect Customer conversational analytics.

choices.title: Implemented consistent tagging standards with controlled vocabularies

helpfulResource.displayText: Optimizing your knowledge base (AWS Contact Center Blog, 2024, written before the Connect Customer AI agents name)

improvementPlan.displayText: Create a controlled vocabulary document that defines all allowable tags, their definitions, and usage guidelines. Enforce tagging through content management tooling and periodic audits. Apply the tags to Connect Customer knowledge base content with the TagResource API so AI agents can filter retrieval by tag, or map them to metadata fields if you bring your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base.

choices.title: Automated taxonomy enforcement through content validation pipelines

improvementPlan.displayText: Build automated validation checks that reject or flag content submissions lacking required taxonomy fields. Integrate with your CMS or content pipeline to ensure every article meets categorization standards before publishing to the knowledge base.

choices.title: Regular taxonomy reviews driven by evolving customer intent data

helpfulResource.displayText: Connect Customer conversational analytics

improvementPlan.displayText: Schedule quarterly taxonomy reviews using conversational analytics and search query logs to identify emerging intents not covered by existing categories. Retire obsolete categories and add new ones based on actual customer demand patterns.

choices.title: Taxonomy mapped to AI retrieval optimization (metadata filters, chunk boundaries)

helpfulResource.displayText: How content chunking works for knowledge bases (AWS Bedrock User Guide)

improvementPlan.displayText: Align your taxonomy structure with how your knowledge base filters and chunks content. In Connect Customer knowledge bases, map categories to the content tags you use for content segmentation. In your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base, map them to metadata fields. Ensure category boundaries inform chunking decisions so that retrieved chunks contain coherent, topic-specific information.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Begin by auditing your existing content and creating a basic taxonomy aligned to your top 20 customer contact reasons. Use Connect Customer conversational analytics to identify the most common intents and build categories around them. Even a simple two-level hierarchy improves AI retrieval quality.

questions.title: How do you ensure content consistency across voice, chat, and self-service channels?
questions.description: Customers interact through multiple channels including voice with agents, chat, and AI-powered self-service. Content must be structured to deliver consistent answers regardless of channel while being optimized for each modality (concise for chat, detailed for self-service, agent-friendly for voice).

helpfulResource.displayText: Generative AI self-service with Connect Customer AI agents

choices.title: Single-source content model with channel-specific rendering rules

helpfulResource.displayText: Connect Customer AI agents self-service

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement a single-source-of-truth content model where each knowledge article exists once but includes structured sections for different channels. Use metadata or content blocks to define what renders in self-service versus what agents see versus what the AI summarizes for chat.

choices.title: Content authored with channel-aware formatting (length, tone, structure)

improvementPlan.displayText: Develop authoring guidelines that specify content requirements per channel. Self-service content should be comprehensive with step-by-step instructions. Chat responses need concise answers under 300 characters. Agent-facing content should include decision trees and policy details.

choices.title: Automated testing validates content renders correctly across all channels

improvementPlan.displayText: Create test suites that verify content displays properly in each channel. Test that AI-generated responses from the same source article are appropriate for chat versus self-service contexts. Use Connect Customer Testing and Simulation to run automated test cases for self-service interactions, and test chat and voice experiences from the Connect Customer admin website, to validate response quality per channel.

choices.title: Channel analytics identify content gaps specific to each modality

helpfulResource.displayText: Connect Customer conversational analytics

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitor per-channel metrics to identify where content fails. Track self-service abandonment rates, chat escalation triggers, and agent handle time by topic. Use conversational analytics to find topics where one channel performs well but another struggles, indicating content format issues.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by inventorying which content is used in which channel today. Identify the top 10 topics that span all channels and restructure those articles first using a single-source model. Test the restructured content in Connect Customer AI agents to validate it produces appropriate responses for both agent assist and self-service use cases.

questions.title: How do you segment and manage content across multiple lines of business or product domains?
questions.description: Organizations with multiple products, brands, or lines of business need clear content boundaries to prevent AI from providing incorrect cross-domain answers. Proper segmentation ensures customers receive information relevant to their specific product or service context.

choices.title: Clear content domain boundaries with explicit LOB ownership mapping

improvementPlan.displayText: Define explicit boundaries between content domains. Map every knowledge article to a specific LOB or product line. Document ownership so each content domain has a responsible team. This prevents cross-contamination where AI retrieves billing content for a technical support query about a different product.

choices.title: Knowledge base scoping aligned to contact routing and queue structure

helpfulResource.displayText: Knowledge base retrieval configuration (multiple knowledge bases and content segmentation)

improvementPlan.displayText: Align your knowledge base structure with your AWS Connect routing configuration. Use separate knowledge bases or tag-based content segmentation so that when a contact is routed to a specific queue, the AI only searches relevant content for that LOB or product domain. Set the AI agent version or session tag filter for each queue from your flow with an AWS Lambda function block.

choices.title: Shared content identified and governed separately from domain-specific content

improvementPlan.displayText: Identify content that spans multiple LOBs (for example, general policies, company information) and manage it in a shared content layer. Establish governance rules for who can modify shared content versus domain-specific content. Ensure shared content is tagged appropriately for cross-domain retrieval.

choices.title: Automated cross-domain conflict detection prevents contradictory answers

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement automated checks that detect when content from different domains provides contradictory information about overlapping topics. Flag conflicts for human review and establish precedence rules for resolution. This is critical when products share similar features with different implementations.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Begin by mapping your organizational structure to content domains. List all LOBs, products, and services, then assign existing content to each domain. Identify content that does not cleanly fit one domain and establish a governance process for shared content. Scope retrieval by domain with separate knowledge bases or content segmentation: tags on Connect Customer knowledge base content, or metadata filters if you bring your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base.

questions.title: How do you identify and address content coverage gaps against customer intents?
questions.description: Content coverage gaps occur when customers ask questions that have no corresponding knowledge article or when existing content is insufficient to generate accurate AI responses. Systematic gap analysis ensures your knowledge base evolves with customer needs.

helpfulResource.displayText: Connect Customer conversational analytics

choices.title: Systematic mapping of customer intents to available content using contact analytics

helpfulResource.displayText: Connect Customer conversational analytics

improvementPlan.displayText: Use conversational analytics to extract the top customer intents from actual contacts. Map each identified intent to existing knowledge articles. Intents without corresponding content represent gaps that need new article creation. Prioritize based on contact volume and business impact.

choices.title: AI retrieval failure analysis identifies queries with no good matches

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable AI agent event logging to AWS CloudWatch Logs and review cases where the AI could not find relevant content: answers that report insufficient information, recommendations with a LOW relevance level, and results that agents mark as not useful. Aggregate these failed queries to identify systematic content gaps. Create a backlog of content to author based on retrieval failure frequency.

choices.title: Agent escalation patterns analyzed to find self-service content gaps

helpfulResource.displayText: Self-service with Connect Customer AI agents

improvementPlan.displayText: Analyze patterns in self-service to agent escalations. When customers consistently escalate on specific topics, it indicates the self-service content is insufficient. Create detailed content for high-escalation topics and test that AI responses reduce escalation rates.

choices.title: Proactive content creation ahead of product launches and policy changes

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish processes to create knowledge content before new products launch or policies change. Integrate with product and policy teams to receive advance notice. Author and test content in staging environments so it is ready when customers begin asking questions about new offerings.

choices.title: Quantitative coverage score tracked and reported to stakeholders

improvementPlan.displayText: Define a coverage score metric (for example, percentage of top 100 intents with corresponding content rated as sufficient). Track this score over time and report it to leadership. Set targets for coverage improvement and allocate content authoring resources accordingly.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start with conversational analytics to identify your top 50 customer contact reasons. For each reason, check if adequate knowledge content exists. Create a simple spreadsheet tracking intent, content availability, and content quality. This gap map becomes your content creation backlog prioritized by contact volume.

questions.title: How do you author content optimized for AI retrieval and response generation?
questions.description: Content written for human readers does not always perform well when used by AI systems for retrieval-augmented generation. AI-optimized content requires specific structural patterns, clarity standards, and formatting that helps embedding models and language models produce accurate responses.

helpfulResource.displayText: Optimizing your knowledge base (AWS Contact Center Blog, 2024, written before the Connect Customer AI agents name)

choices.title: Content structured with clear headings, concise paragraphs, and explicit answers

helpfulResource.displayText: Optimizing your knowledge base (AWS Contact Center Blog, 2024, written before the Connect Customer AI agents name)

improvementPlan.displayText: Restructure content to lead with the answer, followed by supporting details. Use descriptive headings that match how customers phrase questions. Keep paragraphs to 2-3 sentences. Avoid burying critical information in long narrative blocks. This improves both chunking quality and response generation accuracy.

choices.title: Authoring guidelines specify AI-friendly patterns (Q&A format, decision trees, step lists)

improvementPlan.displayText: Create authoring style guides that emphasize AI-friendly patterns. Use question-and-answer format for FAQ content. Present procedures as numbered steps. Use decision trees for complex logic. Avoid ambiguous pronouns, implied context, and references to other sections without restating key information.

choices.title: Content tested against AI retrieval and generation quality before publishing

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish a testing step in the content workflow where authors verify that new or updated content produces accurate AI responses. Test with representative customer queries in a staging environment. Iterate on content structure until retrieval quality and response accuracy meet defined thresholds.

choices.title: Content avoids ambiguity, jargon, and implicit assumptions that confuse AI models

improvementPlan.displayText: Train content authors to write explicitly. Define all acronyms, avoid internal jargon unless necessary, state assumptions clearly, and provide context within each article rather than relying on readers having read other articles. AI models perform better with self-contained, unambiguous content.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Begin by selecting 10 high-traffic knowledge articles and rewriting them following AI-optimization principles: lead with the answer, use clear headings, write concise paragraphs, avoid ambiguity. Test the rewritten articles in Connect Customer AI agents and compare response quality to the originals. Use the results to develop your authoring standards.

questions.title: How do you manage multilingual content and localization for AI-powered experiences?
questions.description: Organizations serving customers in multiple languages must ensure AI-powered content experiences work effectively across all supported languages. This includes translation quality, cultural localization, and ensuring AI retrieval works correctly with multilingual knowledge bases.

choices.title: Defined language strategy with primary and secondary language support tiers

improvementPlan.displayText: Define which languages are fully supported (all content translated, tested with AI), partially supported (key content only), and unsupported. Base decisions on customer demographics and contact volume by language. Document the strategy so teams understand content obligations for each language tier.

choices.title: Translation workflow integrated into content lifecycle with quality assurance

improvementPlan.displayText: Embed translation into your content publishing workflow. When source content is created or updated, trigger translation processes automatically. Include native-speaker review for quality assurance. Ensure translated content is tested with AI retrieval to verify the translations produce accurate responses.

choices.title: Separate knowledge bases or metadata scoping per language for retrieval accuracy

improvementPlan.displayText: Configure language-specific knowledge bases or use metadata filtering to ensure AI retrieves content in the correct language. Mixing languages in a single unscoped knowledge base can cause cross-language retrieval errors. Align language scoping with your contact routing language detection.

choices.title: Cultural localization beyond translation (examples, formatting, regulatory differences)

improvementPlan.displayText: Go beyond word-for-word translation. Adapt examples to local context, use region-appropriate formatting (dates, currencies, units), and account for regulatory differences between markets. Content that feels natural in the target language produces better customer experiences and higher AI response quality.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by analyzing your customer base by language to determine which languages require support. For each required language, assess current content availability and quality. Begin with your top 20 contact reasons and ensure those are properly translated and tested with AI retrieval in each supported language.

questions.title: How do you enable content personalization and contextual relevance in AI responses?
questions.description: Effective AI-powered customer experiences deliver personalized responses based on customer context such as product ownership, account status, history, and preferences. Content must be structured to support contextual filtering and personalization at retrieval time.

choices.title: Content tagged with customer segment and product applicability metadata

improvementPlan.displayText: Tag every knowledge article with metadata indicating which customer segments and products it applies to. Use these tags as retrieval filters so the AI only surfaces content relevant to the specific customer's context. This prevents generic responses when specific guidance is available.

choices.title: Customer context passed to AI at query time for scoped retrieval

helpfulResource.displayText: Add customer data to an AI agent session

improvementPlan.displayText: Configure your AWS Connect contact flows to pass customer context (product owned, account tier, region, history) to Connect Customer AI agents at query time. Use this context to filter knowledge base results and personalize AI responses based on the specific customer situation.

choices.title: Conditional content sections address different customer scenarios within articles

improvementPlan.displayText: Structure articles to address multiple customer scenarios with clearly labeled sections (for example, For Enterprise customers versus For individual customers). This helps AI select the appropriate section when generating responses based on the customer context provided.

choices.title: Personalization effectiveness measured through response relevance metrics

improvementPlan.displayText: Track whether personalized responses result in better outcomes than generic ones. Measure response relevance, customer satisfaction, and resolution rates for contacts where personalization was applied versus not. Use these metrics to justify investment in content personalization and identify where it adds the most value.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by identifying the top customer context attributes that change the correct answer (for example, product tier, account age, region). For your highest-volume intents, review whether the answer varies by these attributes. Where it does, add metadata tags and restructure content to support contextual retrieval.

questions.title: How do you manage knowledge article interconnection and cross-referencing?
questions.description: Complex customer issues often require information from multiple knowledge articles. Effective cross-referencing helps AI systems understand relationships between topics and provide comprehensive answers that draw from related content without creating circular dependencies or conflicts.

choices.title: Explicit relationship mapping between related articles using structured metadata

improvementPlan.displayText: Define relationship types (prerequisite, related, supersedes, child-of) and map connections between articles using structured metadata. This helps AI understand when it needs to combine information from multiple sources and which articles provide complementary versus overlapping information.

choices.title: Self-contained articles that include essential context without requiring other articles

helpfulResource.displayText: Optimizing your knowledge base (AWS Contact Center Blog, 2024, written before the Connect Customer AI agents name)

improvementPlan.displayText: Author each article to be self-contained for its core topic. Include essential context within the article rather than relying on readers following links. AI retrieval works best with self-contained chunks. Provide cross-references for additional detail but ensure the primary answer is complete within each article.

choices.title: Circular reference detection prevents conflicting or infinite retrieval loops

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement validation that detects circular references and conflicting information across related articles. When Article A references Article B which references Article A, ensure there is no contradictory information that could confuse AI response generation. Establish clear precedence rules.

choices.title: Cross-reference strategy accounts for chunking boundaries in AI retrieval

helpfulResource.displayText: How content chunking works for knowledge bases (AWS Bedrock User Guide)

improvementPlan.displayText: Design cross-references to work within the constraints of chunk-based retrieval. Include critical related information in the same chunk or connect it clearly through metadata. Avoid relying on readers to follow links: each query returns only a limited number of chunks (set by maxResults in Connect Customer AI agent knowledge base settings), so the linked content may not be among them.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Audit your most-referenced articles to understand cross-referencing patterns. Identify articles that are frequently incomplete without their referenced content. Prioritize making those articles self-contained. Then establish a relationship metadata schema to help AI understand content connections.

questions.title: How do you prioritize content creation and improvement based on business impact?
questions.description: With limited content authoring resources, organizations must prioritize which content to create, update, or optimize first. Effective prioritization uses data on business impact including contact volume, revenue impact, customer effort, and AI performance metrics.

choices.title: Content prioritized using quantitative impact scoring (volume, cost, satisfaction)

helpfulResource.displayText: Connect Customer conversational analytics

improvementPlan.displayText: Develop a content priority score combining contact volume (how often customers ask), cost impact (average handle time multiplied by volume), and satisfaction impact. Use conversational analytics data to quantify these factors. Focus content improvement efforts on articles with the highest combined impact score.

choices.title: AI performance data (retrieval failures, low-relevance results, negative feedback) drives content backlog

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitor AI retrieval quality signals, such as answers that report insufficient information, low-relevance recommendations, guardrail blocks, and results agents mark as not useful, and use them to set content improvement priorities. Topics where AI consistently underperforms indicate content that needs restructuring or expansion. Feed these signals into your content backlog alongside volume-based priorities.

choices.title: Content investment aligned to strategic business objectives and cost reduction goals

improvementPlan.displayText: Connect content strategy to business objectives such as self-service containment targets, handle time reduction goals, or customer satisfaction improvements. Prioritize content that directly supports these objectives. Report content investment ROI to justify ongoing resource allocation.

choices.title: Regular reprioritization cadence responds to changing business conditions

improvementPlan.displayText: Review and adjust content priorities at least monthly. Business conditions change with product launches, seasonal patterns, and market events. A static priority list becomes stale. Use automated dashboards showing content performance trends to quickly identify emerging priorities.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by pulling your top 20 contact reasons from conversational analytics or your routing data. Calculate the total monthly cost of each (volume times average handle time times cost per minute). Rank content improvement efforts by this cost metric. This simple approach ensures you address the highest-impact content first.

questions.title: How do you manage content deduplication and resolve conflicting information?
questions.description: Duplicate or conflicting content causes AI systems to generate inconsistent or incorrect responses. When multiple articles address the same topic with different information, the AI may randomly select between them, leading to unpredictable customer experiences and eroded trust.

choices.title: Automated duplicate detection using semantic similarity analysis

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement automated scanning that detects semantically similar content across your knowledge base. Use embedding-based similarity to find articles covering the same topic even when worded differently. Flag potential duplicates for human review and consolidation.

choices.title: Clear source-of-truth designation for each topic with conflict resolution rules

improvementPlan.displayText: For every topic, designate a single authoritative source article. When conflicts are detected, the authoritative source takes precedence. Document conflict resolution rules (for example, newer policy supersedes older, product-specific supersedes general). Ensure AI retrieval prioritizes authoritative sources.

choices.title: Regular deduplication sweeps as part of content maintenance cycles

improvementPlan.displayText: Schedule quarterly deduplication reviews where content teams scan for redundant or conflicting articles. Merge duplicates into single authoritative articles, redirect or archive obsolete versions, and update cross-references. Track the duplicate rate as a content health metric.

choices.title: Content publishing workflow prevents duplicate creation through topic claiming

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement a topic claiming mechanism in your content workflow. Before authoring new content, require authors to search for existing articles on the same topic. If content exists, route them to update the existing article rather than create a new one. This prevents duplicates at the source.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Begin by identifying your most common customer question and searching your knowledge base for all articles that could answer it. If you find multiple articles with different answers, you have a conflict problem. Consolidate to a single authoritative article. Repeat for your top 20 topics to address the most impactful duplicates first.

questions.title: How do you design chunking strategies appropriate for each content type?
questions.description: Chunking determines how content is divided for embedding and retrieval. Different content types (FAQs, procedures, policies, troubleshooting guides) require different chunking approaches to preserve semantic coherence and ensure retrieved chunks contain complete, useful information.

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases chunking strategies

choices.title: Content-type-specific chunking strategies (fixed, semantic, hierarchical) defined

helpfulResource.displayText: Chunking strategies for AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases

improvementPlan.displayText: Define chunking strategies per content type. For FAQs, store each Q&A pair as its own document and choose no chunking, or use small fixed-size chunks. Long procedures benefit from hierarchical chunking, which pairs large parent chunks with smaller child chunks to balance context and precision. Policies may need semantic chunking to keep related clauses together. Set the strategy in chunkingConfiguration when you create a Connect Customer knowledge base with the CreateKnowledgeBase API, or in the data source of your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base. Test each strategy against retrieval quality.

choices.title: Chunk size and overlap parameters tuned through retrieval quality testing

helpfulResource.displayText: FixedSizeChunkingConfiguration (AWS Connect Customer API Reference)

improvementPlan.displayText: Systematically test different chunk sizes (200-1000 tokens) and overlap percentages (10-25%) against a set of representative queries. Measure retrieval precision and recall for each configuration. Smaller chunks improve precision but may lose context. Larger chunks preserve context but reduce precision.

choices.title: Metadata preserved across chunk boundaries for context retention

improvementPlan.displayText: Ensure each retrieved chunk carries its source context (article title, section heading, product, category). When the AI retrieves chunks independently, this context helps the AI generate accurate responses. In Connect Customer knowledge bases, tag each content item with the TagResource API (not available for web crawler content) and repeat key context in section text. In your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base, attach a metadata file to each AWS S3 document, or add chunk-level metadata with a custom transformation AWS Lambda function during ingestion.

choices.title: Custom chunking logic handles special formats (tables, code blocks, decision trees)

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement custom chunking for content that does not chunk well with standard approaches. Tables should not be split across chunks. Code blocks and step-by-step procedures should remain intact. Decision trees need their complete logic in a single chunk. Use custom transformation logic in your ingestion pipeline.

choices.title: Regular chunk quality audits verify retrieval coherence post-ingestion

improvementPlan.displayText: After ingestion, audit a sample of chunks to verify they contain coherent, useful information in isolation. Check that no critical context was lost at chunk boundaries. Run test queries and inspect the retrieved chunks for completeness. Schedule these audits after any chunking configuration changes.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start with your knowledge base's default chunking and test retrieval quality with 20 representative customer queries. Note where retrieved chunks are incomplete or incoherent. Use these observations to select appropriate chunking strategies, which you set with the CreateKnowledgeBase API for a Connect Customer knowledge base or in the data source of your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base. Begin with semantic chunking for narrative content and fixed-size for structured Q&A content.

questions.title: How do you design and implement metadata enrichment and tagging for your knowledge base?
questions.description: Rich metadata enables precise retrieval filtering, contextual scoping, and improved relevance ranking. A well-designed metadata schema allows AI systems to narrow search results based on customer context, content attributes, and business rules.

helpfulResource.displayText: Knowledge base retrieval configuration (content segmentation with tags and metadata fields)

choices.title: Comprehensive metadata schema defined covering content, business, and operational attributes

improvementPlan.displayText: Design a metadata schema that includes content attributes (topic, subtopic, content type, language), business attributes (product, LOB, customer segment, region), and operational attributes (owner, last reviewed date, confidence level). Document the schema and enforce it during content ingestion.

choices.title: Metadata used as retrieval filters to scope AI searches by context

helpfulResource.displayText: Create AI agents in Connect Customer (knowledge base configuration and content tag filters)

improvementPlan.displayText: Filter retrieval at query time. For Connect Customer knowledge bases, tag content and apply tag filters: a contentTagFilter in the AI agent knowledge base configuration, a session tag filter set with the UpdateSession API, or a filter override in an orchestration AI agent's Retrieve tool. If you bring your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base, filter on its metadata fields in the Retrieve tool. Pass customer context (product, language, segment) as filter criteria so retrieval only returns relevant content. This improves precision for organizations with diverse content.

choices.title: Automated metadata extraction and enrichment during content ingestion

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement automated metadata extraction in your ingestion pipeline. Use AI classification to auto-tag content with topics, products, and sentiment. Extract structural metadata (headings, sections) automatically. This reduces manual tagging burden and ensures consistent metadata quality across all content.

choices.title: Metadata quality validation prevents ingestion of poorly tagged content

improvementPlan.displayText: Add validation steps to your ingestion pipeline that reject content missing required metadata fields. Check metadata values against controlled vocabularies. Flag content with inconsistent or suspicious metadata for human review. Poor metadata quality undermines all downstream filtering and retrieval.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by defining the minimum required metadata fields for your use case: content type, product or LOB, language, and last updated date. Apply these fields to your existing content and configure basic metadata filtering in your knowledge base. Even simple filtering improves retrieval relevance.

questions.title: How do you measure and test retrieval quality (precision and recall)?
questions.description: Retrieval quality directly determines AI response accuracy. Without systematic testing of precision (are retrieved results relevant?) and recall (are all relevant results found?), teams cannot identify or fix retrieval problems that lead to incorrect or incomplete AI responses.

choices.title: Test dataset of queries with labeled relevant documents for precision and recall measurement

improvementPlan.displayText: Build a golden test dataset containing 50-100 representative customer queries, each labeled with the correct knowledge articles that should be retrieved. Run these queries against your knowledge base and measure precision (relevant results / total results) and recall (relevant results found / total relevant articles). Track these metrics over time.

choices.title: End-to-end response quality evaluation beyond retrieval (answer accuracy, completeness)

improvementPlan.displayText: Measure not just retrieval quality but end-to-end response quality. Even with correct retrieval, the AI may generate inaccurate or incomplete answers. Evaluate response accuracy, completeness, and relevance using human review or automated evaluation frameworks. Track response quality alongside retrieval metrics.

choices.title: Automated regression testing catches quality degradation after changes

improvementPlan.displayText: Run your test dataset automatically after any change to the knowledge base (new content, chunking changes, model updates). Compare results against baseline metrics to detect regression. Block deployments that degrade retrieval quality below acceptable thresholds. Integrate into your CI/CD pipeline.

choices.title: Production monitoring with real query analysis identifies emerging quality issues

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitor production queries for retrieval quality signals. Track the percentage of queries with no results, queries with low similarity scores, and queries that lead to escalation or negative feedback. Set alerts for quality degradation patterns that may not be caught by pre-defined test datasets.

choices.title: Quality metrics feed back into chunking, embedding, and content improvement decisions

improvementPlan.displayText: Use retrieval quality data to drive improvement decisions. Low precision suggests chunks are too broad or metadata filtering is insufficient. Low recall suggests content gaps or chunking that fragments relevant information. Connect quality metrics to specific actionable improvements.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by collecting 20 common customer queries and manually identifying which articles should be retrieved for each. Run these queries against your knowledge base and check if the correct articles appear in the top results. This simple manual test reveals obvious retrieval problems and establishes a baseline for improvement.

questions.title: How do you integrate multiple data sources into your knowledge base architecture?
questions.description: Contact center knowledge often resides in multiple systems including CMS platforms, wikis, ticketing systems, product databases, and policy repositories. A well-designed connector architecture ensures all relevant sources are integrated while maintaining data quality and freshness.

choices.title: Data source inventory with connector health monitoring and SLAs

improvementPlan.displayText: Maintain a complete inventory of all data sources feeding your knowledge base. For each source, document the connector type, sync frequency, data format, and owner. Monitor connector health with alerts for sync failures. Define SLAs for how quickly source updates must appear in the knowledge base.

choices.title: Standardized ingestion pipeline with data transformation and normalization

helpfulResource.displayText: Initial set-up for AI agents (supported content types and knowledge base integrations)

improvementPlan.displayText: Build a standardized ingestion pipeline that normalizes content from diverse sources into a consistent format. Handle format differences (HTML, PDF, Markdown, JSON) with appropriate parsers. Apply consistent metadata enrichment regardless of source. This ensures uniform retrieval quality across all content sources.

choices.title: Source priority and conflict resolution when multiple sources cover same topic

improvementPlan.displayText: Define source priority rules for when multiple data sources contain content on the same topic. Establish which source is authoritative for each content domain. Implement conflict detection that flags when different sources provide contradictory information requiring human resolution.

choices.title: Incremental sync with change detection minimizes unnecessary reprocessing

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement incremental synchronization that detects and processes only changed content rather than full re-ingestion. Use change timestamps, content hashes, or source system webhooks to identify updates. This reduces processing cost, speeds sync times, and minimizes disruption to the knowledge base during updates.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Begin by listing all systems where contact center knowledge currently resides. Prioritize integration based on content value and query frequency. Start with your primary CMS or knowledge management system using a Connect Customer knowledge base integration (AWS S3, Microsoft SharePoint Online, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk, or web crawler), or bring your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base if you use orchestration AI agents. Add additional sources incrementally once the primary integration is stable and quality-tested.

questions.title: How do you ensure content freshness and timely synchronization?
questions.description: Stale content in knowledge bases leads to incorrect AI responses that erode customer and agent trust. Content freshness mechanisms ensure the knowledge base reflects current policies, procedures, and product information with minimal delay between source updates and retrieval availability.

choices.title: Defined freshness SLAs per content category with automated sync scheduling

improvementPlan.displayText: Define freshness requirements per content category. Policy changes may need near-real-time sync. Product documentation may tolerate daily updates. Define SLAs (for example, critical policy changes reflected within 1 hour) and configure sync schedules accordingly. Monitor SLA compliance with automated alerting.

choices.title: Event-driven sync triggered by content changes rather than just scheduled intervals

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement event-driven synchronization where content changes in source systems trigger immediate ingestion pipeline runs. Use webhooks, change data capture, or event bus patterns to detect updates in real time. This ensures critical updates appear in the knowledge base without waiting for the next scheduled sync window.

choices.title: Stale content detection and automated flagging or removal

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement automated detection of stale content based on last-review dates, content age, and source system status. Flag or temporarily suppress content past its review date. Alert content owners when their articles require freshness verification. Consider confidence degradation for aged content.

choices.title: Sync validation confirms content integrity after each synchronization cycle

improvementPlan.displayText: After each sync cycle, validate that content was ingested correctly. Check document counts, verify sample content matches source, and confirm metadata integrity. Detect sync failures that result in missing or corrupted content. Automated validation prevents silent freshness degradation.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by identifying how frequently your most critical content changes and how long delays between updates and knowledge base reflection currently take. Confirm that the sync frequency of each Connect Customer integration meets that need (Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Zendesk integrations default to hourly). Add monitoring that alerts when sync fails, and check lastContentModificationTime from the GetKnowledgeBase API to confirm when content last changed. Over time, move high-priority content categories to event-driven updates.

questions.title: How do you select and manage vector stores and embedding models?
questions.description: The choice of embedding model and vector store affects retrieval quality, latency, cost, and scalability. Connect Customer knowledge bases manage embeddings and the search index for you, so these decisions apply only when you bring your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base, which works only with orchestration AI agents. Base them on content characteristics, query patterns, performance requirements, and long-term operational considerations. If you use only Connect Customer knowledge bases, mark this question as not applicable.

choices.title: Embedding model selected based on evaluated performance against domain-specific content

improvementPlan.displayText: Evaluate multiple embedding models against your specific content domain. Test retrieval quality with your golden query dataset across different models (for example, Amazon Titan Text Embeddings and Cohere Embed). Domain-specific content may perform differently across models. Select based on measured quality rather than generic benchmarks.

choices.title: Vector store selected based on scalability, latency, and cost requirements

improvementPlan.displayText: Choose your vector store based on specific requirements: AWS OpenSearch Serverless for flexible scaling, AWS Aurora with pgvector for existing PostgreSQL infrastructure, or Pinecone for specialized vector operations. Evaluate latency at expected query volumes, cost at expected data volumes, and operational complexity.

choices.title: Embedding model versioning strategy for upgrades without quality regression

improvementPlan.displayText: Plan for embedding model upgrades since newer models frequently outperform older ones. Define a versioning strategy that allows you to re-embed content with new models, run quality comparisons, and migrate without downtime. Consider maintaining dual indexes during transition periods to prevent quality regression.

choices.title: Dimension and quantization choices balance quality, cost, and performance

improvementPlan.displayText: Understand the tradeoffs between embedding dimensions, quantization, and storage costs. Higher dimensions generally improve quality but increase storage and latency costs. Quantization reduces storage but may slightly reduce precision. Test these tradeoffs with your specific content to find the optimal balance.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start with a Connect Customer knowledge base, where the service manages embeddings and the search index, and measure retrieval quality as your baseline. If you need your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base (orchestration AI agents only), consider an AWS Bedrock managed knowledge base, which uses a service-managed embedding model by default, and confirm it works with your Connect Customer integration. Evaluate custom embedding models or vector stores only when measured quality gaps justify them.

questions.title: How do you implement multi-tenant and access-scoped knowledge base architectures?
questions.description: Organizations often need to restrict knowledge access based on agent role, department, customer tier, or security clearance. Multi-tenant architectures ensure that AI only retrieves content that the current user or customer context is authorized to access.

choices.title: Access scoping model defined with clear rules for who can access what content

improvementPlan.displayText: Define your access scoping requirements: Which content is universal? Which is restricted by role, department, or clearance level? Document the access model with clear rules. Map these rules to technical implementation (separate knowledge bases, metadata-based filtering, or query-time access checks).

choices.title: Technical implementation enforces scoping at retrieval time (not just display time)

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement access scoping at the retrieval level, not just the display level. If restricted content is retrieved but filtered after retrieval, it still impacts AI response generation. Use separate knowledge bases per access scope or metadata filters applied before the semantic search to prevent unauthorized content from influencing responses.

choices.title: Tenant isolation prevents data leakage between organizational boundaries

improvementPlan.displayText: For multi-tenant deployments (BPOs, shared services), implement strong isolation between tenants. Use separate knowledge bases at minimum, and consider separate Connect Customer domains, which do not share integrations or customer data with each other (each Connect Customer instance associates with one domain). Treat tag and metadata filters as scoping, not isolation. Test that queries from one tenant cannot retrieve content belonging to another tenant under any circumstances.

choices.title: Access scope changes propagate immediately to prevent stale permissions

improvementPlan.displayText: When access permissions change (employee role change, content reclassification), ensure the change takes effect immediately in the knowledge base. Design your scoping implementation to evaluate permissions at query time rather than embedding permissions at ingestion time, which would require re-ingestion on every permission change.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by documenting what content access restrictions exist in your organization today. Identify content that should only be accessible to specific roles or departments. Implement basic scoping with separate knowledge bases per access tier, then use content segmentation for more granular control: tags on Connect Customer knowledge base content, or metadata fields on your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base.

questions.title: How do you design knowledge base high availability and disaster recovery?
questions.description: Knowledge base availability directly impacts contact center operations. If AI cannot retrieve content, agents lose real-time assistance and self-service channels fail completely. HA and DR design must account for the knowledge base, vector store, embedding service, and all dependent components.

choices.title: Availability requirements defined with RPO and RTO targets for knowledge base services

improvementPlan.displayText: Define recovery point objective (RPO - maximum acceptable data loss) and recovery time objective (RTO - maximum acceptable downtime) for your knowledge base services. These targets should align with your contact center SLAs. A 4-hour RTO may be acceptable for self-service but a 15-minute RTO may be required for agent assist.

choices.title: Multi-AZ or multi-region deployment for knowledge base components

improvementPlan.displayText: Connect Customer provides active-active resilience within an AWS Region, so Connect Customer knowledge bases need no Availability Zone design from you. For critical workloads that need cross-Region recovery, use Connect Customer Global Resiliency, and note that its list of replicated resources does not include AI agents, AI prompts, AI guardrails, or knowledge bases, so define those as code and deploy them in the replica Region. If you bring your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base, which operates regionally, confirm the redundancy of any vector store you manage and plan regional failover if required.

choices.title: Graceful degradation strategy when knowledge base is partially or fully unavailable

improvementPlan.displayText: Design fallback behaviors for knowledge base outages. Options include routing to experienced agents, serving cached responses for common queries, displaying static FAQ content, or transparently escalating to human support. Ensure contact flows handle knowledge base timeouts and errors gracefully without breaking.

choices.title: Regular DR testing validates recovery procedures work within defined targets

improvementPlan.displayText: Conduct regular disaster recovery tests simulating knowledge base failures. Verify that failover procedures work, recovery completes within RTO targets, and data loss stays within RPO limits. Document runbooks for each failure scenario and ensure operations teams are trained on recovery procedures.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by understanding the business impact of knowledge base unavailability. Calculate the cost per minute of your contact center operating without AI assistance. Use this to set RPO and RTO targets. Connect Customer is resilient within its AWS Region, so focus first on a simple fallback plan for outage scenarios, such as flow branches that route contacts to agents when AI responses fail, and document how to recreate AI agent resources in another Region if your targets require it.

questions.title: How do you optimize search with hybrid retrieval, reranking, and filtering?
questions.description: Pure vector similarity search is sensitive to query phrasing and struggles with exact matches such as product names and error codes. Hybrid search that combines semantic and keyword matching, query reformulation or reranking, and targeted filtering improve retrieval accuracy for real-world contact center queries. Connect Customer knowledge bases support hybrid search, tag filters, and query reformulation prompts. Reranking applies when you control retrieval, such as with your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base.

choices.title: Hybrid search combining semantic similarity with keyword matching implemented

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement hybrid search that combines vector similarity (semantic understanding) with keyword matching (exact term matching). This handles cases where pure semantic search misses specific product names, error codes, or policy numbers. For Connect Customer knowledge bases, set overrideKnowledgeBaseSearchType to HYBRID in the AI agent knowledge base configuration. If you bring your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base, hybrid search requires a vector store with a filterable text field, such as AWS OpenSearch Serverless.

choices.title: Reranking applied to improve result ordering after initial retrieval

improvementPlan.displayText: Apply a reranking step after initial retrieval where your retrieval path supports it. If you call AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases directly, you can apply a reranker model in Retrieve and RetrieveAndGenerate requests. Connect Customer AI agent knowledge base settings offer tag filters, result count, and search type but no reranker, so for native knowledge bases tune those settings instead. Reranking is most valuable when initial retrieval returns many candidates and you need the best ones ranked at the top.

choices.title: Query understanding and expansion improve retrieval for ambiguous or short queries

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement query understanding to handle ambiguous or overly brief customer queries. Expand short queries with context from the conversation. Resolve ambiguous terms using customer context. Consider query reformulation to generate multiple retrieval queries from a single customer question for broader recall.

choices.title: Metadata filtering applied pre-retrieval to reduce search space and improve precision

improvementPlan.displayText: Apply metadata filters before semantic search to constrain the search space. Filter by product, language, content type, or customer segment based on known context. Pre-filtering reduces noise and improves precision by eliminating irrelevant content before similarity matching occurs.

choices.title: Search configuration tuned per use case (agent assist versus self-service versus analytics)

improvementPlan.displayText: Different use cases have different optimal search configurations. Agent assist may need high recall (show more options). Self-service needs high precision (show the best answer). Analytics queries may need different relevance thresholds. Tune search parameters per use case rather than using a single global configuration.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by testing hybrid search against pure semantic search with your golden query dataset. For Connect Customer knowledge bases, set overrideKnowledgeBaseSearchType to HYBRID in the AI agent knowledge base configuration. For your own AWS Bedrock knowledge base, request hybrid search at query time on a supported vector store. Then add basic tag or metadata filtering using product or content type. These two changes typically provide the largest retrieval quality improvement with minimal effort.

questions.title: How do you ensure knowledge base performance and scalability?
questions.description: Knowledge base performance directly impacts customer experience through response latency and contact center efficiency through cost. The architecture must scale with growing content volumes and query loads while maintaining consistent response times during peak contact periods.

choices.title: Performance baselines established with latency targets per operation type

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish performance baselines for key operations: query latency (p50, p95, p99), ingestion throughput, and index update propagation time. Define acceptable targets (for example, sub-500ms query latency at p95). Monitor against these baselines continuously and investigate deviations promptly.

choices.title: Load testing validates performance at peak concurrent query volumes

improvementPlan.displayText: Conduct load testing simulating peak contact center volumes. Model concurrent queries based on your maximum simultaneous contacts multiplied by AI interaction frequency. Verify the knowledge base maintains acceptable latency under load. Test scaling behavior and identify throughput limits before they impact production.

choices.title: Auto-scaling or provisioned capacity handles traffic spikes without degradation

improvementPlan.displayText: Plan capacity for traffic spikes at each layer you control. Contact centers experience predictable daily patterns and unpredictable surges. Connect Customer knowledge bases are managed, so review the Connect Customer AI agents service quotas, including API rate limits, and request increases ahead of peak periods. If you run your own vector store behind an AWS Bedrock knowledge base or custom retrieval service, ensure its scaling policies react fast enough to prevent latency degradation during sudden traffic increases.

choices.title: Content growth planning ensures architecture scales with expanding knowledge bases

improvementPlan.displayText: Plan for content growth by projecting knowledge base size increases over 12-24 months. Verify your vector store and search infrastructure can handle the projected scale. Test retrieval quality and latency at projected content volumes. Some architectures degrade as content grows, requiring proactive capacity planning.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by measuring current query latency in production. Set initial targets based on user experience requirements (agents cannot wait more than 2 seconds for AI suggestions). Implement basic monitoring and alerting for latency breaches. Then plan load testing based on your peak hour contact volumes to identify scalability limits.

questions.title: How do you engineer and manage system prompts for AI interactions?
questions.description: System prompts define the AI persona, behavioral constraints, response format, and domain boundaries. Well-engineered prompts ensure consistent, brand-appropriate, and accurate responses while poorly designed prompts lead to off-brand, verbose, or incorrect AI behavior.

helpfulResource.displayText: Create AI prompts in Connect Customer

choices.title: System prompts define clear persona, tone, behavioral boundaries, and response format

helpfulResource.displayText: Create AI prompts in Connect Customer

improvementPlan.displayText: Design system prompts that explicitly define the AI persona (role, name, personality), communication tone (professional, friendly, empathetic), behavioral boundaries (what topics to avoid, when to escalate), and response format (length, structure, use of lists versus paragraphs). Test prompts with diverse query types.

choices.title: Version-controlled prompts with change management and rollback capability

improvementPlan.displayText: Store system prompts in version control with change history. Require review and approval for prompt changes. Maintain the ability to quickly rollback to previous prompt versions if changes cause quality regression. Track which prompt version is active in each environment (development, staging, production).

choices.title: Context-specific prompts vary by channel, queue, or interaction type

improvementPlan.displayText: Create different system prompts for different contexts. Self-service may need a conversational helper persona. Agent assist may need a concise information retriever persona. Different product lines may need different domain expertise framing. Attach each prompt to its own AI agent, then set the AI agent version per contact from your AWS Connect flows with an AWS Lambda function block, based on routing context.

choices.title: Prompt effectiveness measured and optimized through systematic testing

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish a prompt testing framework that evaluates response quality across a diverse set of test scenarios. Measure accuracy, helpfulness, tone consistency, and instruction following. Use A/B testing to compare prompt variations. Iterate based on data rather than intuition alone.

choices.title: Prompt injection defenses prevent customer inputs from overriding system instructions

helpfulResource.displayText: Create AI guardrails for AI agents (Connect Customer admin guide)

improvementPlan.displayText: Design system prompts with defense against prompt injection attacks where customer messages attempt to override system instructions. Use instruction hierarchy, input sanitization, and the Prompt Attack content filter in a Connect Customer AI guardrail to help stop customers from manipulating AI behavior through crafted inputs.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by documenting what your AI should and should not do in plain language. Convert these requirements into a structured system prompt with clear sections for persona, constraints, and response format. Test the prompt with 20 diverse customer queries and refine based on observed behavior. Store the prompt in version control from day one.

questions.title: How do you ensure AI responses are grounded in source content and prevent hallucination?
questions.description: Hallucination occurs when AI generates plausible-sounding but incorrect information not supported by the knowledge base. In contact centers, hallucinated responses can provide wrong policy information, incorrect procedures, or fabricated product details, causing serious customer and compliance issues.

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS Bedrock Guardrails contextual grounding checks

choices.title: Contextual grounding checks validate responses against retrieved source content

helpfulResource.displayText: Create AI guardrails for AI agents (Connect Customer admin guide)

improvementPlan.displayText: Add a contextual grounding check to a Connect Customer AI guardrail and attach it to AI agents that answer from knowledge base content, such as answer recommendation and manual search, to validate that responses are supported by the retrieved content. Orchestration AI agents do not support contextual grounding policies, so for agentic self-service rely on prompt instructions, source citations, and testing. Configure grounding thresholds appropriate for your use case. Higher thresholds reduce hallucination risk but may also block valid responses that paraphrase source content.

choices.title: System prompts explicitly instruct the AI to only use provided context and cite sources

improvementPlan.displayText: Include explicit instructions in system prompts directing the AI to only answer based on provided knowledge base content. Instruct it to say it does not know when information is not in the retrieved context. Require source citation so responses can be traced back to specific articles. This reduces but does not eliminate hallucination risk.

choices.title: Fallback behavior defined for queries without sufficient knowledge base support

improvementPlan.displayText: Define what the AI should do when it cannot find relevant content to answer a question. Options include acknowledging uncertainty, offering to connect to a human agent, suggesting alternative topics it can help with, or providing a general response with a clear disclaimer. Never allow the AI to fabricate answers to fill gaps.

choices.title: Hallucination detection monitoring identifies and alerts on ungrounded responses

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement monitoring that detects potential hallucinations in production. Compare AI responses against retrieved source chunks using automated similarity or entailment checks. Alert on responses with low grounding scores. Use sampling-based human review to validate automated detection accuracy and identify emerging hallucination patterns.

choices.title: Regular hallucination testing with adversarial queries that tempt fabrication

improvementPlan.displayText: Regularly test your AI with queries designed to tempt hallucination: questions about topics not in the knowledge base, requests for specific numbers or dates, and queries that mix real and fictional information. Verify the AI correctly identifies its knowledge boundaries and does not fabricate answers.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by adding a contextual grounding check with moderate thresholds to a Connect Customer AI guardrail for AI agents that answer from knowledge base content (orchestration AI agents do not support this check). Update system prompts to explicitly instruct the AI to only use provided context. Test with 10 questions that are not in your knowledge base and verify the AI correctly declines to answer rather than fabricating responses.

questions.title: How do you configure content filters to block harmful or inappropriate content?
questions.description: Content filters protect against the AI generating or responding to harmful, toxic, violent, sexual, or otherwise inappropriate content. In customer-facing contact center applications, effective content filtering helps prevent brand damage and protects vulnerable customers.

helpfulResource.displayText: Create AI guardrails for AI agents (Connect Customer admin guide)

choices.title: Content filters configured for hate, insults, sexual, violence, misconduct, and prompt attack, plus a profanity word filter

helpfulResource.displayText: Block harmful words and conversations with content filters (AWS Bedrock User Guide)

improvementPlan.displayText: Create a Connect Customer AI guardrail and configure content filters across all harmful content categories: hate, insults, sexual, violence, misconduct, and prompt attack. Use word filters to block profanity. Set filter strengths appropriate for customer-facing interactions (typically high strength for all categories). Apply filters to both input (customer messages) and output (AI responses).

choices.title: Filter strengths tuned to balance safety with legitimate use case needs

improvementPlan.displayText: Tune filter strengths based on your use case. Healthcare contact centers may need to allow medical terminology that could trigger overly aggressive filters. Financial services may need to discuss fraud scenarios. Test filters against legitimate conversation samples to ensure they do not block valid interactions while maintaining safety.

choices.title: Blocked content handling provides appropriate user-facing fallback responses

improvementPlan.displayText: Design fallback responses for when content filters block AI output. Instead of error messages or silence, provide helpful alternatives such as offering to connect to a human agent, suggesting rephrasing, or redirecting to appropriate support channels. The fallback experience should feel natural, not punitive.

choices.title: Filter effectiveness monitored with false positive and false negative tracking

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitor content filter performance by tracking false positives (legitimate content blocked) and false negatives (harmful content that passes through). Review blocked interaction logs regularly to identify filter tuning needs. Track the percentage of interactions impacted by filters to understand operational impact.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Create a Connect Customer AI guardrail immediately with content filters at high strength across all categories, and attach it to your AI agents. This provides baseline protection for customer-facing AI. Then test with sample interactions from your domain to check for false positives that need tuning. Content filtering is a minimum safety requirement for production deployment.

questions.title: How do you configure denied topics to prevent AI from engaging on restricted subjects?
questions.description: Denied topics prevent the AI from engaging in conversations about subjects outside its intended scope or that pose business risk. This includes competitor discussions, legal advice, off-brand topics, speculative financial guidance, and any subject matter the organization has determined should not be handled by AI.

helpfulResource.displayText: Create AI guardrails for AI agents (Connect Customer admin guide)

choices.title: Comprehensive denied topic list defined based on business risk and compliance requirements

helpfulResource.displayText: Block denied topics to help remove harmful content (AWS Bedrock User Guide)

improvementPlan.displayText: Work with legal, compliance, and business teams to define topics the AI must not engage with. Common denied topics include: specific legal advice, financial investment recommendations, competitor product comparisons, political opinions, medical diagnoses, and internal company strategy. Configure these as denied topics in a Connect Customer AI guardrail, which supports up to 30 denied topics.

choices.title: Denied topic definitions include example phrases and variations for reliable detection

improvementPlan.displayText: For each denied topic, write a crisp, unambiguous definition of up to 200 characters, without instructions or exceptions, and add sample phrases that customers might use, covering direct requests, indirect approaches, and common variations. AWS Bedrock guardrails accept up to five sample phrases per topic, and a clear definition improves detection accuracy. Test with adversarial phrasings that attempt to circumvent detection.

choices.title: Graceful deflection responses guide customers to appropriate alternative channels

improvementPlan.displayText: Design deflection responses that acknowledge the customer's need while redirecting appropriately. Instead of simply refusing, offer alternatives: transfer to a specialist agent, provide a phone number for specific departments, or suggest appropriate self-service channels. The experience should be helpful, not frustrating.

choices.title: Regular denied topic review updates the list as business and regulatory needs evolve

improvementPlan.displayText: Review your denied topics list quarterly or when business conditions change. New regulations may require additional restrictions. Product changes may open previously denied topics. Emerging risks (new scam patterns, trending misuse) may need rapid additions. Maintain an approval process for changes to the denied topics list.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by identifying topics that would create business or compliance risk if the AI discussed them. Consult with legal and compliance teams. Configure at minimum: no legal advice, no financial advice, no medical diagnoses, no competitor recommendations. Add industry-specific restrictions based on your regulatory environment.

questions.title: How do you detect and redact personally identifiable information (PII) in AI interactions?
questions.description: Contact center AI interactions frequently contain PII including names, addresses, social security numbers, credit card numbers, and account identifiers. Proper PII handling prevents sensitive data from being stored in logs, used in model training, or exposed in responses inappropriately.

helpfulResource.displayText: Create AI guardrails for AI agents (Connect Customer admin guide)

choices.title: PII entity types defined and sensitive information filters configured in guardrails

helpfulResource.displayText: Remove PII from conversations by using sensitive information filters (AWS Bedrock User Guide)

improvementPlan.displayText: Identify all PII types that may appear in your contact center interactions. Configure sensitive information filters in a Connect Customer AI guardrail to detect and handle each type: SSN, credit card numbers, bank accounts, health IDs, email addresses, phone numbers, physical addresses. Choose between masking (replacing with placeholders) and blocking for each type based on use case.

choices.title: PII handling strategy differentiates between input redaction and output prevention

improvementPlan.displayText: Define separate strategies for PII in inputs versus outputs. Input PII (customer provides their SSN) may need masking before it reaches the AI model. Block output PII (the AI should never include SSNs in responses). Connect Customer AI guardrails apply one action, Block or Mask, per PII type or regex to both inputs and responses, and blocking a type also blocks customer messages that contain it, so choose the action per type and handle direction-specific needs outside the guardrail, such as redacting input before it reaches the AI agent.

choices.title: Custom regex patterns detect organization-specific sensitive identifiers

improvementPlan.displayText: Configure custom regex patterns in guardrails for organization-specific sensitive data that standard PII detection may not cover: internal account numbers, policy IDs, employee identifiers, or custom reference numbers. Test patterns against real data samples to ensure detection accuracy without false positives.

choices.title: PII handling audited regularly to verify no leakage in logs, analytics, or responses

improvementPlan.displayText: Conduct regular audits of AI interaction logs, analytics pipelines, and stored conversations to verify PII is not leaking past redaction controls. Check that masked data remains masked in downstream systems. Test the end-to-end data flow to confirm PII handling is consistent across all touchpoints.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Add sensitive information filters to a Connect Customer AI guardrail immediately for common PII types (SSN, credit cards, bank accounts) and attach it to your AI agents. Each type takes one action, Block or Mask, for both customer inputs and AI responses, so test each choice against conversations where customers must share that data. This provides baseline protection. Then audit your interaction logs to verify PII is not appearing in stored data.

questions.title: How do you implement and tune contextual grounding checks?
questions.description: Contextual grounding checks verify that AI responses are derived from the retrieved source content rather than from the model's training data, and that they are relevant to the customer query. In Connect Customer, you add these checks to AI guardrails, but orchestration AI agents do not support them. Proper tuning balances grounding strictness (preventing hallucination) against response flexibility (allowing natural language generation). If you use only orchestration AI agents, mark this question as not applicable and assess grounding in the question on grounding AI responses in source content and preventing hallucination.

helpfulResource.displayText: Contextual grounding checks in AWS Bedrock Guardrails

choices.title: Grounding threshold configured based on tested accuracy versus coverage tradeoff

helpfulResource.displayText: Contextual grounding checks

improvementPlan.displayText: Test different grounding threshold values (0 to 0.99. A threshold of 1 is invalid because it blocks all content) against your golden test dataset. Higher thresholds block more hallucination but also block more valid paraphrased responses. Find the threshold that minimizes hallucination while maintaining acceptable response rates. Monitor the block rate in production to detect if thresholds need adjustment.

choices.title: Relevance check confirms responses answer the customer query, and retrieval tuning keeps irrelevant context out

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable the relevance check alongside the grounding check. Grounding measures whether a response is supported by the retrieved source, and relevance measures whether it answers the customer query, so a response can be grounded yet irrelevant. Set the relevance threshold from test data. The check does not filter retrieved chunks, so keep irrelevant excerpts out of the source by tightening content tag filters and maxResults in your AI agent knowledge base configuration.

choices.title: Different grounding strictness applied for different content risk levels

improvementPlan.displayText: Apply stricter grounding for high-risk content (financial policies, legal terms, safety procedures) and more relaxed grounding for low-risk content (general product descriptions, greeting messages). Connect Customer supports up to three custom AI guardrails and one guardrail per AI agent, so attach a stricter guardrail to the AI agents that serve high-risk queues or lines of business, and select the AI agent version for each contact from your flow.

choices.title: Grounding check results logged and analyzed to improve content and retrieval quality

improvementPlan.displayText: Log grounding check results to understand why responses are blocked or flagged. Frequent grounding failures on specific topics indicate content quality issues (content not matching how the AI wants to phrase responses) or retrieval issues (wrong content retrieved). Use this data to improve both content authoring and retrieval configuration.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by adding a contextual grounding check with a moderate threshold (around 0.7) to a Connect Customer AI guardrail, and attach it to AI agents that answer from knowledge base content, since orchestration AI agents do not support the check. Monitor the block rate over one week. If too many valid responses are blocked, lower the threshold slightly. If hallucinations get through, raise it. Use the first week of data to find your optimal operating point.

questions.title: How do you design AI self-service to human agent escalation paths?
questions.description: Effective escalation design ensures customers can smoothly transition from AI self-service to human agents when the AI cannot resolve their issue. Poor escalation experiences cause customer frustration, repeated information requests, and eroded trust in the AI channel.

helpfulResource.displayText: Generative AI self-service with Connect Customer AI agents

choices.title: Clear escalation triggers defined (topic types, failed resolution attempts, customer signals, explicit requests)

helpfulResource.displayText: AI self-service with Connect Customer AI agents

improvementPlan.displayText: Define explicit conditions that trigger escalation to a human agent: the AI cannot find relevant content, customer expresses frustration, topic is in escalation-required list, multiple failed resolution attempts, or customer explicitly requests a human. Write these conditions into the instructions of the Escalate Return to Control tool and your orchestration prompt, then route on the returned tool name in your AWS Connect flow with a Check contact attributes block.

choices.title: Context preservation passes conversation history and customer data to the receiving agent

helpfulResource.displayText: Use agentic self-service (custom Escalate tool with context)
