Stale runbooks are dangerous during incidents when teams follow outdated procedures that no longer work correctly.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by documenting your three most critical operational procedures: how to deploy content to production, how to respond when AI quality drops, and how to escalate issues. Write procedures that a new team member could follow without prior knowledge. Keep them in a shared, accessible location. Expand coverage over time.

questions.title: How do you approach capacity planning and scaling for AI content systems?
questions.description: AI content systems must scale with contact center growth, seasonal traffic patterns, and expanding content volumes. Capacity planning ensures the system handles peak loads without degradation while avoiding over-provisioning that wastes cost during low-traffic periods.

choices.title: Capacity requirements modeled based on contact volume projections and growth plans

improvementPlan.displayText: Model capacity requirements using contact volume projections, AI interaction rates, content growth plans, and seasonal patterns. Include peak hour multipliers and growth buffers. Plan capacity 6-12 months ahead to avoid being surprised by gradual growth. Update models quarterly with actual usage data to improve projection accuracy.

choices.title: Auto-scaling configured for variable workloads with tested scaling policies

improvementPlan.displayText: Configure auto-scaling for the components you run yourself. Connect Customer manages capacity for its AI features, so track its quotas instead. Define scaling policies based on relevant metrics (query rate, latency, queue depth). Test that scaling responds quickly enough to traffic spikes. Verify scale-down behavior does not cause instability. Load test at projected peak to validate scaling limits, and get written AWS approval at least two weeks before any load test that touches your AWS Connect instance.

choices.title: Cost optimization balanced against performance through right-sizing analysis

improvementPlan.displayText: Regularly analyze resource utilization to right-size components. Over-provisioned resources waste cost. Under-provisioned resources degrade performance. Use utilization data to identify opportunities for cost optimization without sacrificing performance. Consider reserved capacity for baseline loads and on-demand for peaks.

choices.title: Service quota limits monitored and increased proactively before reaching thresholds

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitor AWS service quotas (API rate limits, provisioned throughput, concurrent requests) relative to your usage. Request quota increases proactively when usage approaches 70% of limits rather than waiting for throttling. Track quota utilization as a regular operational metric. Hitting quotas during peak traffic causes immediate customer impact.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by understanding your current AI system utilization during peak hours. Identify the component closest to its capacity limit. Set up monitoring for utilization metrics and alerts at 70% of capacity. Request service quota increases for any limits you may reach within 3 months. Build a simple capacity model based on contact volume growth rate.

questions.title: How do you manage AI model and service updates from AWS?
questions.description: AWS continuously updates AI services including new model versions, service feature releases, and API changes. Managing these updates requires awareness of changes, impact assessment, testing before adoption, and planned migration to avoid disruption while benefiting from improvements.

choices.title: AWS service update monitoring with impact assessment for each relevant change

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitor AWS service announcements, release notes, and deprecation notices for all services in your AI content architecture. Assess the impact of each relevant change on your system. Categorize changes as: breaking (requires action), beneficial (worth adopting), or neutral (no action needed). Maintain awareness of upcoming changes.

choices.title: Model version pinning with controlled upgrade process

improvementPlan.displayText: Pin model and configuration versions wherever you control them rather than relying on defaults that may change unexpectedly. In Connect Customer, choose the model in your custom AI prompts and reference published AI prompt and AI agent versions instead of system defaults. Fully managed AI features change their underlying models over time, so monitor them after AWS updates. When upgrading model versions, follow a controlled process: test the new version against your evaluation dataset, compare quality and performance metrics, then deploy through staging to production with monitoring.

choices.title: Testing and validation required before adopting any service or model update

improvementPlan.displayText: Require testing before adopting any update to AI services or models. Even minor version updates can change behavior in ways that impact your specific use case. Run your golden test dataset against the updated service. Compare results to current baselines. Only proceed to production when results meet or exceed current performance.

choices.title: Deprecation planning ensures migration before end-of-life deadlines

improvementPlan.displayText: Track service and model deprecation timelines and plan migrations well in advance of end-of-life dates. Do not wait until deprecation deadlines force emergency migrations. Start migration planning at least 3 months before deprecation. Test replacement services thoroughly. Communicate timeline to stakeholders.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by subscribing to AWS service update notifications for AWS Connect, AWS Bedrock, and any vector store you run, such as AWS OpenSearch Serverless. Document which specific model versions and API versions you currently use. Set a monthly reminder to check for relevant updates. When updates are available, test in staging before applying to production.

questions.title: How do you train and enable content teams for AI-powered content operations?
questions.description: Content teams working with AI-powered systems need skills beyond traditional knowledge management. They must understand how AI consumes content, how to optimize for retrieval, how to interpret AI quality metrics, and how to use new tools and workflows effectively.

choices.title: Training curriculum covers AI content principles, tools, and workflows

improvementPlan.displayText: Develop a training curriculum covering: how AI retrieval-augmented generation works, how to write content optimized for AI, how to use content management and quality tools, how to interpret performance metrics, and how to troubleshoot common content quality issues. Provide hands-on exercises with real examples from your system.

choices.title: Onboarding program for new content team members includes AI-specific training

improvementPlan.displayText: Include AI-specific content training in the onboarding program for new team members. New hires should understand the AI system architecture, content quality requirements, and operational workflows before they begin authoring. Pair new authors with experienced mentors during their first content contributions. Track onboarding effectiveness through quality metrics.

choices.title: Ongoing skill development keeps teams current with AI capabilities and best practices

improvementPlan.displayText: Provide ongoing learning opportunities as AI capabilities and best practices evolve. Schedule monthly knowledge sharing sessions, share relevant industry updates, encourage experimentation with new features, and allocate time for professional development. AI content operations is a rapidly evolving field requiring continuous learning.

choices.title: Content team performance feedback includes AI quality outcomes

improvementPlan.displayText: Include AI quality outcomes in content team performance feedback. Show authors how their content performs in AI interactions: retrieval rates, response quality when their content is used, and customer satisfaction scores. This creates a feedback loop connecting authoring practices to business outcomes and motivates quality improvement.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start with a basic training session explaining how AI uses knowledge base content and what makes content AI-friendly. Show real examples of well-performing versus poorly-performing content from your system. Provide a one-page quick-reference guide for AI-optimized authoring. Even basic awareness training improves content quality.

questions.title: How do you manage vendor and service dependencies for AI content systems?
questions.description: AI content systems depend on multiple AWS services and potentially third-party vendors. Managing these dependencies requires understanding the dependency chain, monitoring health, planning for failures, and maintaining the ability to adapt if dependencies change or become unavailable.

choices.title: Complete dependency map documenting all services, versions, and criticality levels

improvementPlan.displayText: Create and maintain a dependency map listing every service your AI content system relies on: AWS Bedrock (specific models and features), AWS Connect, knowledge base infrastructure, embedding services, vector stores, content sources, and any third-party services. Document version dependencies, criticality level, and alternatives for each.

choices.title: Dependency health monitoring with alerting for service degradation

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitor the health of all dependencies continuously. Use AWS Health Dashboard, service-specific health checks, and synthetic monitoring to detect dependency issues. Alert when dependencies degrade before they impact your system. Understanding whether an issue is in your system or a dependency speeds up troubleshooting.

choices.title: Fallback strategies defined for critical dependency failures

improvementPlan.displayText: Define fallback strategies for each critical dependency. If the AI model is unavailable, can you fall back to a simpler model or cached responses? If the knowledge base is down, can you serve static FAQ content? If a content source is unavailable, does cached content remain usable? Test fallback scenarios regularly.

choices.title: Vendor lock-in assessed and mitigated for strategic flexibility

improvementPlan.displayText: Assess vendor lock-in risk for each dependency. Consider: how difficult would it be to switch? What is the migration cost? Are there viable alternatives? For high lock-in dependencies, evaluate mitigation strategies such as abstraction layers, portable content formats, and multi-vendor capable architectures. Balance lock-in risk against operational simplicity.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by listing all AWS services and external dependencies your AI content system uses. For each, note what happens to your system if that dependency becomes unavailable. Identify your most critical dependency (usually the AI model or knowledge base) and design a basic fallback. Monitor AWS Health Dashboard for your dependent services.

questions.title: How do you drive continuous experimentation and optimization of AI content experiences?
questions.description: AI content systems offer many optimization levers (prompts, chunking, models, content structure, guardrail settings) but intuition alone cannot determine optimal configurations. Systematic experimentation with hypothesis testing and measurement enables data-driven optimization of the entire system.

choices.title: Experimentation framework enables controlled testing of changes with measurement

improvementPlan.displayText: Build an experimentation framework that enables controlled testing of configuration changes. Support A/B testing (split traffic between variants), before/after measurement (compare metrics around a change), and staged rollouts (gradually increase exposure to changes). Ensure statistical rigor in interpreting results to avoid false conclusions.

choices.title: Optimization backlog maintained with hypotheses prioritized by expected impact

improvementPlan.displayText: Maintain a backlog of optimization hypotheses: content restructuring ideas, prompt variations, chunking adjustments, model alternatives, and configuration changes. Prioritize hypotheses by expected impact and effort. Run experiments against top hypotheses continuously. This ensures optimization effort is directed at highest-value improvements.

choices.title: Experiment results documented and shared to build organizational knowledge

improvementPlan.displayText: Document all experiment results including hypotheses that did not improve performance. Build organizational knowledge about what works and what does not for your specific content domain. Share learnings across teams. This prevents repeated testing of disproven hypotheses and accelerates future optimization efforts.

choices.title: Innovation time allocated for exploring new approaches and emerging capabilities

improvementPlan.displayText: Allocate dedicated time for exploring new AI capabilities, emerging best practices, and innovative approaches. AI technology evolves rapidly with new model capabilities, service features, and techniques emerging frequently. Teams without innovation time fall behind and miss opportunities to improve their systems.

choices.title: Optimization ROI tracked to demonstrate value of continuous improvement investment

improvementPlan.displayText: Track the ROI of your optimization program: measure improvements in quality, cost, and customer satisfaction attributable to experiments and optimizations. Report this ROI to leadership to justify continued investment in experimentation. Quantify the cumulative value of all successful optimizations over time to demonstrate compounding returns.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Start by identifying one optimization you want to test (for example, a prompt change, a chunking adjustment, or a content restructuring). Measure current performance on relevant metrics. Make the change. Measure again after sufficient volume. Compare results. This simple before/after approach demonstrates the value of experimentation and builds momentum for a more systematic program.
